validity.recommendation: keep row; add note that it is the Ukrainian side of the Bereg interconnector with Hungary
validity.researcher_notes: The line is real. Ukrainian Wikipedia describes the Berehove to Beregdaroc interconnector, a 2020 joint notice from the Hungarian and Ukrainian operators names both physical points, and a Ukrainian export capacity table lists 'Ужгород-Берегово' with 2 pipes. None of the four sources cited on the sheet's wiki page names this branch. It is not a duplicate of P1489 or P3063, which cross into Slovakia. The row is presented as domestic but the crossing is cross-border with Hungary.

validity.researcher_notes: The sheet has 13 bcm per year. Ukrainian Wikipedia says up to 13 for the 1987 crossing. A Ukrainian export capacity table says 11 for this line. The 2020 notice implies far higher technical capacity at the point. These are different measures and do not agree.

verifications.note: Hungarian operator's 2024 ten-year plan: 400,000 cm/h of firm capacity from Hungary to Ukraine at the Hungary-Ukraine border point, 17 June 2024 to 30 June 2025. Names the Beregdaroc point.
Argus, 2025: Ukraine's operator sold entry capacity at the Bereg virtual point on the Hungary border for August 2025; the point was almost sold out.

fills.researcher_notes: Two separate publishers dated 2024 and 2025 show gas still moving through the Berehove to Beregdaroc border crossing. The crossing is the end of this line. Neither source uses the name Uzhhorod-Berehove, so the link to this row rests on the crossing.
